_comment: Checkstack tuned seccomp profile for the script sandbox. Purpose: permit the UNPRIVILEGED user-namespace + bubblewrap (rootless) syscalls the script sandbox needs, while staying TIGHTER than `seccomp=unconfined`. The runtime default seccomp profile (Docker/containerd) blocks unprivileged `clone(CLONE_NEW*)` / `unshare` / `setns` / `mount` / `pivot_root` (gated behind CAP_SYS_ADMIN), which makes rootless bwrap fail and the secure fail-closed sandbox default refuse every run. This profile keeps `defaultAction: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW` (so the full Bun/Node + sh + bwrap + nftables syscall set is permitted) and explicitly ERRNOs the genuinely dangerous syscalls the runtime default denies (kernel module load/unload, reboot, kexec, swap, clock/domainname mutation, raw BPF/perf, ptrace of others, etc.). VALIDATION STATUS: VALIDATED in-container against a real syscall trace of the full DEFAULT_SANDBOX_PROFILE flow (shell + ESM runners + bwrap + prlimit + nft, FS+net+privilege+resources incl. the per-run fork-bomb cap): every needed syscall is permitted (ZERO denials of a required syscall), the flow runs to success with all layers `enforced` and zero downgrades, and a dangerous syscall is genuinely blocked (e.g. `delete_module` returns EPERM=errnoRet:1 under this profile vs ENOSYS unconfined). It is the SHIPPED default referenced from the Dockerfiles, docker-compose.yml, and the deploy/k8s example. The profile must be paired with a `/proc` unmask (Docker `--security-opt systempaths=unconfined` / Kubernetes `procMount: Unmasked`) so bwrap can mount a FRESH /proc inside the namespace; that unmask is safe because the sandboxed script runs in a fresh PID+mount namespace as non-root and never sees the host /proc (verified: a script cannot read host process environ). Fallback if a host cannot mount this file: `seccomp=unconfined` + `systempaths=unconfined`; if neither relaxation is possible, set the global policy to `degrade`.

syscalls._comment: Namespace + rootless-bwrap syscalls: explicitly ALLOWED (the runtime default gates these behind CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which a non-root supervisor does not hold). These are exactly what unprivileged user namespaces + bwrap mount/pivot_root/net-namespace setup need.

DENIED: the dangerous syscalls the runtime default profile blocks. Keeping these blocked is what makes this profile tighter than `unconfined`. Covers kernel-module load/unload, reboot, kexec, swap, clock/domainname/hostname mutation, NUMA/mempolicy abuse, raw BPF, kernel perf, and the legacy/obsolete calls.
